body:
> V5.2.7 Verify that the application sanitizes, disables, or sandboxes user-supplied Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) scriptable content, especially as they relate to XSS resulting from inline scripts, and foreignObject.

XSS > content execution

comments.body:
Additionally to get rid of XSS...

What does "disables" mean in this requirement? Previously discussed 5+ years ago https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/455

Sandboxing is covered by other requirement V50.6.1:
> V50.6.1 Verify that security controls are in place to prevent browsers from rendering content or functionality in HTTP responses in an incorrect context (e.g., when an API, a user-uploaded file or other resource is requested directly). Possible controls could include: not serving the content unless HTTP request header fields, such as Sec-Fetch-*, indicate it is the correct context, Content-Security-Policy: sandbox, Content-Disposition: attachment, etc.

In general I think the requirement needs some focus change - at the moment it is mixed to accepting the SVG (sanitization) and serving/using the SVG (sandboxing). The requirement is in sanitization section and must only focus on sanitization part.

Also the question is, should the sanitization part happen when accepting the file or when using the file. Note, that using SVG can cause also problems for server-side components that renders it (SSRF) and is not only limited to malicious content exection impact via browser.

> Also the question is, should the sanitization part happen when accepting the file or when using the file

Never. You *validate* user uploaded files when they are first uploaded using multiple validation techniques (anti malware, content introspection, etc) and if the file does not conform to those validation techniques you reject them.

*sometimes* you may want to do things like remove EXIF data from images. I would suggest doing that during the initial file upload validation phase and discard the original when that is possible. Sometimes discarding or even modifying the original uploaded file is not possible for a wide variety of reasons based on the type of app.

And there are some situations where additional security checks are needed when using a file, but that depends on what you are doing.

Personally I don't mind and compared to sanitization it is maybe more correct way to handle it, but I'm not sure we can require it as the only acceptable way to solve the situation.

The problem to solve here: user-uploaded svg file
* is processed by the server-side component (for example used when generating a pdf) and causes SSRF
* is served from same-origin scope and HTML, JavaScript, etc can be executed for the victim (if accessed directly with an HTTP request or is included via object tag into the HTML document)

As mentioned in the previous comment, serving files for direct HTTP requests is covered by 50.6.1.

Needs wordsmithing, but direction proposa:
> Verify that user-supplied Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) scriptable content is validated or sanitized to contain only  tags and attributes (such as draw graphics) that are safe for the application,  e.g., do not contain scripts and foreignObject.
This is a good argument Elar, and I agree. I like your changed version.

Any wording checks/improvement for this?

ping @tghosth

> Verify that user-supplied Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) scriptable content is validated or sanitized to contain only tags and attributes (such as draw graphics) that are safe for the application, e.g., do not contain scripts and foreignObject.

Looks good to me
Is this requirement more suitable into V12.2 File Integrity and Content? Or is it expected that an end-user can provide svg syntax via wysiwyg editor? (I would say 5.2.1 covers that)

> While I agree that XSS is incorrect, it has the the benefit of being well known term which is widely understood...

I say that those, who _can only describe_ problem with a term "XSS", can not actually understand the problem or what the "XSS" is.

We don't have any other mention of XSS (at least in requirements) and I can see it as a good thing.

Every requirement need to explain why it exists:
> V5.3.1 Verify that output encoding for an HTTP response, HTML document, or XML document is relevant for the context required, such as encoding the relevant characters for HTML elements, HTML attributes, HTML comments, CSS, or HTTP header fields, to **avoid changing the message or document structure**.

From this issue point of view it is a off-topic, if there is a problem to solve or discuss, please open a separate issue for that. Again, personally I don't see the need for that, and it goes too much to the educative field and it is out of scope for ASVS. As people like to take sentences out of context I highlight that requirements must be understandable.

> > Verify that user-supplied Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) scriptable content is validated or sanitized to contain only tags and attributes (such as draw graphics) that are safe for the application, e.g., do not contain scripts and foreignObject.
> 
> Looks good to me

We discussed that it is best this stays in 5.2. @elarlang to open a PR
